about.heading: Garfield Wang
about.lede: Twenty years, one question: how sound changes human state.
about.bio1: Sound doesn't just reach us — it rearranges us. I've spent twenty years proving it across four mediums: radio, where sound holds attention; music, where it drives emotion; sleep hardware, where it regulates the nervous system; and now voice AI, where it becomes the interface itself.
about.bio2: Now, as founder of Soundario, I build software that senses a listener's state and shapes sound in real time — sound engineered to put a specific person in a specific state.

index.hero.heading: Sound doesn't just reach us. It rearranges us.
index.hero.lede: Twenty years of making sound for people: radio and music first, then a sleep pillow that plays it, a teleprompter that keeps you talking, and now the audio AI underneath.
index.hero.caption: Audio producer, product maker, broadcaster.

index.pilo.title: PILO®
index.pilo.desc: Sound brought into sleep and rest. A music-driven pillow with six international design awards.
index.talktalk.title: Talktalk
index.talktalk.desc: Keeps the script beside the lens so your attention stays on what you're saying. A Phoenix TV (Hong Kong) news anchor: “Smooth, intuitive, never working against you.”
index.aurora.title: AURORA
index.aurora.desc: Audio AI from a single sine wave to Whisper. 99 lessons, every algorithm written by hand in NumPy, the whole course open source under MIT.
index.rbr.title: Run Baby Run®
index.rbr.desc: Cadence music for runners, every step on the beat. Official soundtrack of the Nike Shanghai Marathon, now produced through an AI workflow.
index.practice.heading: The through-line
index.practice.body: On radio I learned that sound holds attention. In music, that it moves people. With PILO I found it can settle a nervous system, and with Talktalk that it can carry a thought. AURORA is me taking the whole stack apart to see how it works. Different products, the same question: what does sound do to a person, and how do you make that on purpose.
